newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday due to rises on the domestic A share markets in active trading, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 16.00 percent from 13.10 percent on Tuesday.
Turnover fell to 6.57 million lots from 13.51 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The rises on the Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets today helped push up the repo rates, with institutions borrowing more money to trade on the share markets," one trader said.
Traders expect the rates to remain at high levels if the A share markets stay bullish.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down due to institutional selling, with prices meeting resistance after rises for the past three days, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 116.61 yuan from 117.33. Volume of the nine-contract market fell to 1.0 million lots from 2.7 million.
"Institutional profit-taking selling was the main factor today," said a trader. "This short-term profit-taking indicated that the market is still weak and lacks the strength to go up."
